tests_evidence.recorded_commit_body:
WebKit Networking on macOS 26.0.1 retains about 5.5 KB per fetch request
and releases nothing when pages reload or connections close. An isolated
WKWebView grew linearly over HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/1.1, with ephemeral and
default data stores alike. Ribbon Field's Networking process reached
8.9 GB after 47 hours at about 16 requests per second across three
windows.

  provider events (item/*, hook/*, diffs, plans, usage, rate limits) no
  longer start an inventory read; provider requests still do.
- Refresh decisions and schedules only when an inventory read starts,
  not on every refresh call that joins a pending read.

A concurrent comparison against the live backend reduced fetches per
window from 483 to 122 in two minutes.

window from 483 to 122 in two minutes.

all_commit_screening.subject: Reduce backend contention behind slow conversation opens
all_commit_screening.body:
Every store operation opened a new SQLite connection, and each new
connection parsed the full schema. Event streams also reread durable
coordination state on every provider delta. With several windows and
running agents, the backend spent most of its CPU parsing schemas and
waiting on SQLite's allocator mutex, so detail reads took 1-3 seconds.

- Reuse one idle store connection per thread. Nested uses get their own
  connection; failed uses are discarded; unfinished cursors are closed
  and factory settings restored before reuse.
- Forward provider events immediately, but read coordination state at
  most once a second per event stream.
- Read a known app conversation's thread and session together when
  opening or refreshing it.
- Block tiling only for conversations whose drafts move into panes while
  their send or image attachment is still in flight.

all_commit_screening.subject: Make sending and opening conversations immediate under agent load
all_commit_screening.body:
Measured on a snapshot of the live database with streaming agents, event-
driven windows and hook writers (scripts/measure_backend_latency.py) and in
a real browser (scripts/measure_interaction_latency.mjs):

- Show a sent message on Enter with Sending, Sent and Not sent states;
  a rejected message returns its text to the composer.
- Accept a send to a loaded idle conversation without reading its whole
  transcript; a conversation believed running still reconciles first.
- Share one thread-list build across concurrent readers for up to one
  second, and app-agent creators for display projections; windows refresh
  the list at most once per second and ignore events that cannot change it.
- Keep Claude Code running when only its instructions' saved thread
  context changed; most messages were paying a full Claude Code start.
- Paint a cached conversation from another project before that project's
  list loads, and reuse unchanged messages when a stream re-renders.
- Index agent-woken turns, which every list build looks up.

Realistic load, installed backend versus this change: send acceptance p50
420 -> 100 ms (max 1734 -> 258 ms), delivery to other windows p50 392 ->
53 ms, list p50 1162 -> 111 ms, backend CPU 93 -> 49 %. Enter -> visible
is 3-11 ms in the browser. Budgets and remaining limits are in
docs/responsiveness.md.

conversations stay paused; their supervisors receive one notice and
may recover them after inspection with a fresh continuation.

counts as retired. Unloading an idle app conversation also ends its
session, which previously let a bystander adopt a live lead's agents.

Preserve the runtime-owned active-turn flag so Close when done accepts the running task, while terminal startup still resets to idle. Cover automatic and explicit close after a delayed startup hook through the HTTP endpoints.
